text: By 2050, many experts predict we will have created Artificial General Intelligence, or AGI. Unlike today's AI, which can only perform specific tasks, AGI would possess human-like reasoning and learning abilities across any field. The potential benefits are enormous: AGI could accelerate medical discoveries, solve complex climate problems, and revolutionize education with personalized tutoring. However, serious risks exist. An AGI might make decisions we cannot fully understand or control, and its goals could conflict with human values. Most specialists believe we are still decades away, yet some think AGI could emerge within ten years. Either way, careful research and international cooperation are essential to manage this powerful technology safely.
